meta_title: Preorders · A funding target for every product
meta_description: Every OpenDrone product option has its own public funding target, set at the quantity we order from the supplier. Watch each target fill.
title: A funding target for every product.
lead: The designs are finished. What we need now is the money to order production runs, so every product option has a public target: the quantity we order from the supplier. Your preorder pays for that run, and you can watch each target fill.

s1_body: OpenDrone is an open source FPV platform: flight controller, ESC, receiver, motors and frames, with the design files public.
Development is done. What is missing is money for production, not engineering time. Preorders pay for the supplier orders.
s2_body: Suppliers do not produce single units. Each sets a minimum order quantity, and that quantity is the target for the product option.
When a target is reached we place the supplier order, and the product ships about 10 weeks later. Orders keep coming in after that: they fill the next batch, which gets its own target.
s3_body: Batch 1 of the flight controller and the ESC, 250 of each size, is paid for and in production. It ships late October 2026.
Once batch 1 is gone, the stack gets a funding target like every other product.
s4_body: You pay the full price when you order. Every product sells at a preorder price, 20% under its later price, until its target is reached; the stack keeps it while batch 1 lasts. The product page shows the price that follows.

Shipping is charged at checkout at the rate for your destination zone. Orders to the United States ship duty paid: import duties are calculated and charged at checkout, and there is nothing to pay on delivery.
s5_body: An order ships once, complete. If you order the stack together with a product that is still funding, the whole order waits until everything in it is ready. Order separately if you want the stack sooner.
s6_body: Hardware schedules slip. Supplier lead times move, a component goes out of stock and has to be replaced by an equivalent, and a production run can need rework. When a ship date moves, you get mail with the new date.

A product can also fall short of its target. Targets are set at a quantity we can order, so a product that falls short can still go ahead as a smaller run. Either way, everyone who ordered it gets mail saying what happens next.
s7_body: Incutec BV, a small company in Leuven, Belgium. The same people design the boards, answer the support mail and pack the parcels.
This is not a crowdfunding platform: you order in our own shop, under [our terms](/algemene-voorwaarden), article 7bis.
faq_a1: When you order: the product price, shipping and, for the United States, import duties. Nothing is charged later.
faq_a2: The stack ships late October 2026 while batch 1 lasts. Every other product ships about 10 weeks after its target is reached. Each item shows its ship date on the product page, at checkout and on the order confirmation.
faq_q3: What happens when a target is reached?
faq_a3: We place the supplier order and mail everyone who ordered that product. You hear from us again when the ship date is set and before dispatch.
faq_q4: What if the ship date moves?
faq_a4: You get mail with the new date as soon as we know it.
faq_q5: Do I get one parcel or several?
faq_a5: One. An order ships once, complete, when every item in it is ready.
faq_q6: Do you ship to the United States?
faq_a6: Yes, duty paid. Import duties are calculated from each product's customs classification and charged at checkout, so the carrier asks for nothing on delivery.
faq_a7: No. A preorder pays for the production run of your own order. It carries no interest and gives you no equity, revenue share or other stake in the company.
faq_q8: Where do the numbers on this page come from?
faq_a8: From paid orders in our shop. Each product option counts only its own units, and the numbers refresh every minute.
